name: Is shower tile itself waterproof, or do I need waterproofing underneath it?

mainEntity.name: Is shower tile itself waterproof, or do I need waterproofing underneath it?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. A reliable shower tile installation starts with a properly sloped shower base, suitable solid backing, and a continuous waterproofing system beneath the tile. Tile and grout resist water but are not the primary waterproof barrier. Context: Elite Remodeling & Design coordinates bathroom design, tile selections, and related construction work, so the waterproofing approach should be decided before the tile pattern. Key factors: - Confirm how wall corners, niches, benches, curb, and drain will be sealed. - Ask which membrane and compatible backer system will be used. - Verify that penetrations for valves and showerheads are sealed. Practical guidance: Request a written shower assembly description before demolition or tile ordering. Photograph the waterproofing before it is covered if the project allows. A coordinated bathroom remodeling team can address waterproofing before finish choices lock in the layout.
acceptedAnswer.description: Tile and grout are not the primary waterproof barrier. The shower needs a continuous waterproofing system beneath the tile, properly tied into the drain and sealed around corners, niches, benches, curbs, and plumbing penetrations.
